Plucky

PLUCK-ee · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Plucky is showing spirited courage, especially in facing difficult odds.

The plucky underdog team kept fighting until the final second, even though they trailed by twenty points at halftime.

Worked Example

Everyone expected the tiny startup to fold within a year, but its plucky founders kept pitching investors long after most people would have given up.

Showing spirited, admirable courage especially when the odds are against you is exactly what plucky describes.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

Build the Word

The pieces

root — pluck

root — pluck: courage, spirit (English)

suffix — -y

suffix — -y: characterized by, full of (English)

Put it together

Put it together: Plucky is built from pluck plus the adjective-forming suffix -y. Pluck originally meant to pull or tug at something; oddly, it came to mean 'courage' or 'spirit,' possibly from the older sense of the heart and other organs being 'plucked' from a slaughtered animal. Someone plucky, then, is full of that hardy spirit.

Word Choice

Plucky has a warm, slightly diminutive tone -- it's often used affectionately for an underdog, a child, or a small team, rather than for a large, powerful figure. Compare it with dauntless, which is a grander, more formal word for fearlessness in serious danger.
